---
title: T4 - Networks (Contact transmission)
jupyter: python3
---


Person-to-person transmission is captured by network-mediated interaction. In this tutorial, we will use a random network, where pairings of people are generated at random at each timestep, but the average number of pairings or contacts on each timestep can be specified. 


```{python}
import starsim as ss
import typhoidsim as ty

# Define high-level simulation parameters
pars = dict(
    start    = 2000,          # Starting year
    dur      = ss.years(1),   # Duration of the simulation
    dt       = ss.days(1),    # Timestep of 1 day
    verbose  = 0,             # Do not print details of the run
)

# The population
ppl = ss.People(10_000)

# Person to person transmission
random_p2p = ss.RandomNet(n_contacts=5)

# The disease, with no environmental route (`teer=0`), so all transmission is by contact
typhoid = ty.Typhoid(teer=0)

sim = ss.Sim(
    pars=pars,
    people=ppl, 
    networks=random_p2p,
    diseases=typhoid,
    )
sim.run()
sim.plot()
```

## Contact route: how it currently works

For this particular network, a _target_ individual will be in contact on average with 5 people (called _sources_) on each time step. These sources can be infected or not. If they are infected, the _target_ individual is infected at a rate per contact (`exposure2contact_rate`, per day) that depends on:

- the infectiousness of the source individual, by stage of infection relative to acute (`tpri` for prepatent, `tsri` for subclinical, `tcri` for chronic) -- and their relative transmissibility, `rel_trans`, which interventions can change
- the susceptibility of the _target_ individual, which is reduced by each past infection (by a factor `1 - tppi` per infection), and their relative susceptibility, `rel_sus`

Infections by contact have the prepatent period of a high dose.
